game.name: ecos
game.description: Ecos: grass, grazers and predators on a continuous field, one seat per trophic role. Each seat is a whole species and sets a four-integer doctrine once per generation; the score is integrated biomass, and any role that crashes the others crashes itself a generation later.

tokens.description: One per-seat websocket token, in slot order.

players.description: Policy names, in slot order. Seats never see them.

num_agents.description: Seats. Ecos is a three-seat game.

seed.description: Episode seed; unpinned it is randomised at start.

roleOffset.description: role(slot) = (slot + roleOffset) mod 3. -1 derives it from the seed.

grassGain.description: Unshaded photosynthesis gain per tuft per tick.

minTurnSeconds.description: Floor on wall-clock spacing between generation starts.

episodeTimeoutSeconds.description: Assumed platform kill time; play stops at 60% of it.

playerConnectTimeoutSeconds.description: How long to wait for the three seats before starting anyway.

shutdownGraceSeconds.description: How long /healthz and /global keep answering after the artifacts are written, so hosted certification's post-pod ping lands.

variant.description: Which variant's opening this episode ran. Recorded into the replay's config block so a harsh-spring replay is distinguishable from a standard one.

actionTimeoutSeconds.description: Deadline for one simultaneous generation of player actions.

scores.description: Capped integrated biomass by slot; higher is better.

biomass.description: Mean biomass over the ticks played, by slot.

population.description: Population on the last played tick, by slot.

generations.description: Generations scored. A generation cut short by a collapse is closed, scored against the full denominator and counted here.

ending.description: ten_generations | collapse_grass | collapse_grazers | collapse_predators | deadline | forfeit

player.value:
ecos.player.v2 uses JSON text frames over the websocket named by COWORLD_PLAYER_WS_URL (/player?slot=N&token=T).

On connect the game sends a welcome with protocol, slot, alias, role, generations, and ticksPerGeneration. At each boundary it sends a state with the seat's private observation: role, generation, you, species, history, density, notes, and rules. The same observation is carried as view in a decision frame: {"type":"decision","protocol":"ecos.player.v2","generation":G,"timeout_ms":25000,"view":{...state...}}. All seats receive their decision before any doctrine is applied.

The player replies {"type":"action","generation":G,"source":"llm|scripted|fallback","doctrine":{...four role fields...},"say":"...","notes":"...","latency_ms":N}. Late, duplicate, malformed, or missing actions do not override the current decision. The game validates and clamps each doctrine; an absent action uses steward fallback. Say is capped at 64 runes and notes at 400.

Grass doctrine: seed_threshold 60..200, seed_range 24..240, seed_cost 20..80, crowd_limit 0..6. Grazers: birth_threshold 80..240, bite 2..14, flee_range 0..300, herd 0..100. Predators: birth_threshold 150..400, hunt_range 40..400, rest_energy 0..400, spread 0..100. The game sends a final frame with scores and ending, then the player exits 0.

global.value:
Global spectators connect a websocket to /global and receive the bitworld sprite protocol as binary frames: a layer + viewport message, the sprite definitions (soil tiles, four grass stages, the grazer and predator poses, the sparkle/splash/fade effects and the silent-spring wash), then one object message per living body per frame with stale ids deleted. The broadcast chrome - scorebug, GEN n / 10 clock, doctrine feed, transport, population strip and end-card - rides as the LABEL of the reserved 1x1 sprite id 4090 and is routed straight to the page's onText handler; it is a JSON object with t/mt/ph/pl/sp/mx/st/teams/roster/events, plus lead (the whole-episode population strip, shipped once) and over (the end-card).

GET /client/global serves that page live. Recorded episodes are NOT served by a pod: the replay is one strict-UTF-8 JSON document (protocol ecos.replay.v1) of per-tick state frames, and the static wasm bundle plays it at index.html?replay=<url>. GET /healthz and GET /client/player?slot=N&token=T complete the contract.

readme.value:
Ecos is a three-seat ecology on a 1000x562 continuous field. One seat is the GRASS, one the GRAZERS, one the PREDATORS, and the roles rotate by seed. You are a species, not an individual: your seat may have one body alive or two hundred, and each of them runs the same deterministic kernel.

Once per generation - ten generations of sixty ticks each - a seat submits a DOCTRINE: four whole numbers that reparameterise that kernel for the next sixty ticks. Grass sets when, how far and how expensively it seeds and how much crowding it will tolerate; grazers set when they split, how hard they bite, how early they run and how tightly they herd; predators set when they split, how far they lock on, how fat they must be to rest and how far apart they spread.

Your score is integrated biomass: for each generation, your total biomass over its ticks divided by your reference, capped at 2.0, summed over ten. Higher is better. Energy only flows up the chain, so a level that strips the level below it starves about a generation later - and the episode ends the instant any species reaches zero, with every remaining generation scoring zero for all three seats. Winning means staying in balance.

Each seat is an ordinary player policy over the private state and complete doctrine action. Set PLAYER_PROMPT for a prompt model or PLAYER_SCRIPTED=steward|opportunist for a baseline. The game owns legality, deadlines, results, and replay.

content.value:
# Ecos rules

## The field and the clock

- Continuous field, 1000 x 562 world units, no walls and no obstacles. Bodies are
  clamped to the rectangle; there is no wrap-around.
- One episode = 10 generations x 60 ticks = 600 ticks. Playback is 24 fps, so a
  full replay is 25 seconds of video.
- Every sim quantity is an integer. Headings are brads (0..255) resolved through
  a 256-entry integer sine table, and the RNG is a seeded integer stream, so one
  seed reproduces one replay bit-exactly on any host.

## Seats and roles

| slot | alias   | role when roleOffset = 0 | colour |
|------|---------|--------------------------|--------|
| 0    | Sedge   | grass (producer)         | green  |
| 1    | Bramble | grazers (herbivore)      | yellow |
| 2    | Quill   | predators (carnivore)    | red    |

role(slot) = (slot + roleOffset) mod 3, with roleOffset = seed mod 3 unless the
config pins it. Roles rotate; aliases do not. Seats see ONLY the three aliases -
no policy name, player name or account ever reaches a seat.

## The doctrine

| role      | field           | range   | default |
|-----------|-----------------|---------|---------|
| grass     | seed_threshold  | 60..200 | 100     |
| grass     | seed_range      | 24..240 | 90      |
| grass     | seed_cost       | 20..80  | 40      |
| grass     | crowd_limit     | 0..6    | 3       |
| grazers   | birth_threshold | 80..240 | 90      |
| grazers   | bite            | 2..14   | 10      |
| grazers   | flee_range      | 0..300  | 40      |
| grazers   | herd            | 0..100  | 20      |
| predators | birth_threshold | 150..400| 400     |
| predators | hunt_range      | 40..400 | 140     |
| predators | rest_energy     | 0..400  | 200     |
| predators | spread          | 0..100  | 40      |

A doctrine holds until the next generation. Out-of-range values are clamped and
the decision is recorded as clamped; a missing or non-numeric field is an
invalid reply, retried once and then replaced by the steward doctrine.

## Tick resolution order

1. Grass photosynthesis: gain = clamp(grassGain - neighbours within 55, 0,
   grassGain), then minus 1 metabolism, capped at 200.
2. Grazer sense: crowding within 60, stress = min(2, crowd / 6), distance to the
   nearest predator, whether a tuft is within 16.
3. Grazing: bite min(doctrine.bite, tuft energy) from the nearest tuft; the
   grazer keeps 80% of it.
4. Grazer movement and metabolism: grazing bodies hold still; fleeing bodies run
   at 9 (11 with four or more neighbours) for 2; the rest walk at 6 for 1,
   blending food and herd directions by `herd`.
5. Predator sense: crowding within 60, stress = min(2, crowd / 2), cooldown down
   one.
6. Predator act: above rest_energy it idles for 1; otherwise it locks the nearest
   grazer within hunt_range, kills within 16 once every 12 ticks for
   min(180, 90 + the grazer's energy), chases at 12 for 3, or roams at 7 for 2.
7. Positions are clamped to the field.
8. Deaths: grazers marked eaten (predation), then any body at 0 energy or less
   (starve). Dead bodies are removed before births.
9. Births, grass then grazers then predators, each stopping at its cap. Grass
   seeds seed_range away for seed_cost + 10, or pays 10 and fails when the target
   is already crowded. Grazers and predators split at birth_threshold, both
   halves keeping (energy - 20) / 2.
10. Record the tick's state frame, its events and the population/biomass row.

## Scoring

- Instantaneous biomass B(t) is the total energy of your living bodies.
- References: grass 20000, grazers 4000, predators 3000.
- G(g) = (sum of B(t) over generation g) / (60 x your reference).
- Score = sum over the ten generations of min(G(g), 2.0). Higher is better;
  a balanced ecosystem scores roughly 4..13 per seat.
- The episode ends the instant any species reaches 0. Every remaining generation
  scores 0 for all three seats, so a crash costs its author more than restraint
  would have.

# Fielding a policy in Ecos

`/bin/ecos-player` receives the private `ecos.player.v2` decision and returns one complete doctrine action per generation. The game sends the same observation to any player and owns doctrine validation, fallback, results, and replay.

Set `PLAYER_PROMPT` for the reference Claude policy. Set `PLAYER_SCRIPTED=steward` or `opportunist` for deterministic policies. A missing or failed model call sends the steward fallback action.

The observation contains all three species' populations, biomass, births, starvations and predation counts; a 10x6 density grid per species; the seat's own doctrine, energy, crowding, rules, and notes. It excludes other seats' doctrines, notes, and say text, the seed, and individual body positions.

The action contains `doctrine` with all four role fields, plus `say` and `notes`. Say is spectator-only; notes return to the same player next generation. The game clamps out-of-range fields, caps text at rune boundaries, and uses a steward doctrine if a seat is absent or its action is invalid.

player.name: Ecos Prompt Player
player.description: Prompt player: chooses a complete doctrine from each private decision using PLAYER_PROMPT guidance and a player-owned model credential.

player.name: Ecos Steward Baseline
player.description: The scripted steward: the verified default doctrine plus two closed-loop corrections - recruit when thin, back off when your food is thin. Legal by construction and able to sustain ten generations on every seeded opening.

player.name: Ecos Opportunist
player.description: Deterministic opportunist doctrine policy over the ordinary private observation.

variants.name: Standard meadow
variants.description: Three cogs, ten generations of sixty ticks on a rich opening: 160 tufts, 40 grazers, 10 predators.

variants.name: Harsh spring
variants.description: A leaner opening where restraint matters sooner: fewer grazers and fewer predators start the year, so a role that pushes early has less slack to absorb it.
